title: watch-brief-log-and-contextual-handoff-2029-10-14
content:
Evening watch brief (14 Oct 2029) — contextual handoff and action ledger

Summary:
- Shift window: 16:00 — 00:00 PDT. This doc captures the events observed during the evening watch, what we mitigated, and outstanding follow-ups for the midnight team. Overall platform health: degraded briefly but stabilized to baseline.
- High-level: two related alerts (cache pressure + inference latency regression) produced elevated p95 latency for the hosted-api model pool. No customer-facing outage; some requests saw 3–4x token latency for ~20 minutes.

Incidents observed (chronological):
1) 17:12 PDT — Cache eviction storm detected
   - Alert: cache.evictions.rate > 120/s across redis-shard-2 for 3 consecutive minutes.
   - Triage: spike coincided with increased batch size heuristics on Model-X rollout. See metric spike in Grafana panel 'redis/evicts' (id: panel_12).
   - Immediate action: scaled redis-shard-2 from 4 -> 6 replicas (manual scale via infra-capacity-ctl). Applied TTL tuning (reduced retention for temporary keys created by batcher).
   - Outcome: eviction rate dropped to baseline by 17:28.

2) 17:15 — 17:35 PDT — Inference p95 latency increase for hosted-api (model-x-v2)
   - Alert: api.latency.p95 > 2.5s for route /v1/generate for 20 minutes.
   - Correlation: coincident with cache evictions; congestion in KV cache warming caused more attention recompute. Model variant fallback attempted but some routing sticky sessions pinned to hot machines.
   - Mitigation steps: toggled routing policy to allow region-fallback (temporary) and drained two overloaded workers (IDs: gw-7f3, gw-8a2). Reverted batcher auto-suggested batch size increase (rollback via model-configs).
   - Outcome: p95 returned to ~0.6s after 17:40. No data loss.

Escalations:
- 17:22 PDT: Escalated to infra+runtime (Marisol) due to repeated eviction spikes and concerns about shard hotness. Slack snippet: <#SRE-ops> thread.
- On-call pager: no page to on-call rotation required, we handled through channel escalation.

Runbook gaps & suggested edits (actionable):
- Runbook: 'redis/shard-pressure' currently prescribes auto-scaling at 200 evicts/s. We observed instability at 120/s due to small shard size and bursty TTLs. Suggest lowering the threshold to 100/s for redis-shard-2 and include guidance to check batcher TTL behaviour.
  - Proposed edit: add step to check 'batcher-temp-keys:*' pattern and TTL distribution before scaling.
- Runbook: 'model-routing-fallback' lacks a sanity check for session stickiness; add 'drain-sticky-sessions' steps to avoid hot-worker hang.

Manual mitigations executed (commands & notes):
- infra-capacity-ctl scale --cluster redis-shard-2 --replicas 6  # executed 17:18
- infra-ops set-ttl --pattern 'batcher-temp-keys:*' --ttl 60s  # executed 17:20 (temporary)
- runtimectl drain-worker gw-7f3 --grace 30s --force  # executed 17:23
- routingctl set-policy hosted-api --fallback-enabled true  # executed 17:26

Metrics snapshot at handoff (17:50 PDT):
- api.latency.p50: 120ms
- api.latency.p95: 610ms
- redis.evictions.rate: 8/s
- worker-cpu-avg (model-x pool): 68%
- error-rate (4xx/5xx): 0.03%

Open follow-ups / owners (explicit owners and expectations):
- Marisol Chen — Investigate root cause for TTL bursting in batcher code (linked PRs and telemetry). Expected update: short write-up + possible patch by 2029-10-15 EOD.
- Ravi Gupta — Add 'drain-sticky-sessions' step to routing runbook and propose fallback sanity checks. Target: 2029-10-16.
- Liam O'Connor — Validate scaling thresholds for redis-shard-2 in a QA repro (simulate batcher bursts). Create a short test harness and run by 2029-10-17.
- Asha Patel (owner) — Coordinate post-incident review draft and attach timeline + Grafana snapshots to Confluence page. Draft due 2029-10-16.

Muted alerts & reasoning: (for handoff clarity)
- Alert: redis.evictions.rate on redis-shard-2 (muted until 2029-10-15 02:00) — temporary mute granted to avoid noise during post-mitigation stabilization. If evictions > 200/s re-enable alerts immediately and page SRE lead.

Notes for the midnight team (00:00 — 08:00 watch):
- Primary watchpoint: watch for reappearance of small-window eviction spikes between 00:00—03:00 PDT. If they resume, escalate using the 'redis/shard-pressure' runbook and call out infra lead on-call (Marisol).
- Secondary: p95 regressions on /v1/generate that coincide with high CPU on model-x workers. If p95 crosses 1.2s for >10 minutes, toggle routing fallback to secondary pool (see routingctl docs).
- Triage tip: before draining a worker, check the 'session-heat' dashboard and perform a soft-drain where possible to avoid repeated sticky-session churn.

Retrospective questions (to include in PIR):
- Why did TTL behavior in the batcher deviate from expectations? Was there a recent config change (PR link: gitlab/ai/batcher#876)?
- Should our redis scaling thresholds be pool-specific rather than uniform?
- Do we need an automated 'session-unstick' mechanism in the routing layer?

Attachments to include in PIR:
- Grafana snapshots: redis/evicts (17:00–18:00), api/latency (17:00–18:00), worker-heatmap (16:30–18:00).
- Logs: runtime logs for gw-7f3 and gw-8a2 (17:10–17:40).
- Timeline: brief timeline with exact command timestamps (this doc + shell history attachment).

Misc notes & oddities:
- Observed a surge of small requests (~<10 tokens) from a single IP range — likely a QA client misconfigured to poll too aggressively. Logged IP and rate-limited at edge for now (edge-rate-limit id: erl-1229). Followup for CS/solutions to contact the customer if it's not internal.
- One alert dropped briefly in PagerDuty due to a config mismatch between PD service tags and Grafana rule tags. Ticket filed: JIRA-SRE-3427 (owner: infra team) — see linked_artifacts.

Handoff checklist (completed):
- [x] Key alerts documented with timestamps
- [x] Runbook deltas noted and owners assigned
- [x] Muted alerts annotated with expiration
- [x] Grafana snapshots uploaded to Confluence draft
- [x] Slack thread summarized and pinned to #SRE-ops

Next shift acceptance (for midnight team):
- Please acknowledge receipt in #SRE-ops and post a short 'ack' with ETA for nightly check at 01:00 PDT. If you see reoccurring evictions, page Marisol immediately.

Signed-off-by:
Asha Patel
Senior SRE (evening watch lead)

---
Edit log: 2029-10-15 — added follow-up owners and updated metrics snapshot after final stabilization at 17:50 PDT.
